senses.gloss: To be able to stop or avoid something, used in the negative.
senses.ru: удерживаться, удержаться; не мочь не (в обороте can't help)
examples: I couldn't *help* laughing when he slipped.
She can't *help* the way she sounds on the phone.
The delay was awful, but it couldn't be *helped*.

senses.gloss: To announce or praise something publicly, especially in the press.
examples: Sports writers *herald* every rookie as the next great quarterback.
The drug was *heralded* as a breakthrough.
The papers are already *heralding* the deal as historic.

senses.gloss: To put a computer into a low-power state that saves whatever is open.
senses.ru: переходить в спящий режим, уходить в гибернацию
examples: Set the laptop to *hibernate* instead of shutting it down.
The PC *hibernated* overnight and woke up with every tab still open.
It has been *hibernating* since I closed the lid.

senses.gloss: To dye streaks of someone's hair a lighter color.
examples: She *highlights* her hair every spring.
I got my hair *highlighted* before the wedding.
The stylist is *highlighting* a few strands around her face.

senses.gloss: To raise a price, tax, or rate by a large amount.
examples: The airline plans to *hike* baggage fees again.
The landlord *hiked* our rent by three hundred dollars.
The Fed has *hiked* interest rates twice this year.

senses.gloss: To say something in a sharp, angry whisper.
examples: Don't *hiss* at the kids — just tell them to sit down.
"Keep your voice down," she *hissed* across the table.
The coach was *hissing* instructions from the sideline.

senses.gloss: To get a free ride by standing at the roadside and signaling to drivers.
examples: We *hitched* a ride to the next town.
He *hitches* to work whenever his truck won't start.
They spent the summer *hitching* across the country.

senses.gloss: To sharpen the edge of a blade against a stone.
examples: He *hones* his kitchen knives every Sunday.
The barber *honed* the razor on a leather strap.
She was *honing* the blade while the water boiled.

senses.gloss: To make the loud call of a goose.
examples: Wild geese *honk* all the way down the valley.
Something *honked* out on the pond before dawn.
We could hear the flock *honking* overhead.

senses.gloss: To do what an agreement or promise requires, or to accept something as valid.
examples: The store *honors* competitors' coupons.
The company *honored* the warranty without an argument.
They have *honored* every term of the contract.

senses.gloss: To catch a fish on a hook.
examples: He *hooked* a big trout on his second cast.
She *hooks* more fish than anyone else in the boat.
I've *hooked* something heavy — get the net.

senses.gloss: To capture someone's interest so completely that they cannot stop.
examples: The first episode *hooked* me.
A good opening line *hooks* the reader.
My son is completely *hooked* on chess.

senses.gloss: To shout or laugh loudly, especially in mockery or delight.
examples: The crowd *hooted* when the mascot fell off the bench.
Kids *hoot* and holler on the last day of school.
We were all *hooting* with laughter by the end.

senses.gloss: To keep a website, program, or file on a server so other people can reach it.
examples: That company *hosts* thousands of small blogs.
Our site was *hosted* on a server in Virginia.
They are *hosting* the database themselves now.

senses.gloss: To contain or hold something inside, said of a building or a case.
examples: The old mill now *houses* a museum.
That building *housed* the city archives for a century.
The battery is *housed* in a waterproof case.

senses.gloss: To stay close to someone, waiting and watching in a way that bothers them.
examples: The waiter *hovered* by our table the whole meal.
Stop *hovering* — I can fold the laundry myself.
She *hovers* whenever her son does his homework.

senses.gloss: To hold the mouse pointer over something on a screen without clicking.
examples: *Hover* over the icon to see what it does.
I *hovered* over the link and the address popped up.
A menu opens when the cursor is *hovering* over the image.

senses.gloss: To laugh, shout, or complain very loudly.
examples: The audience *howled* at his impression of the mayor.
Critics *howl* every time ticket prices go up.
We were *howling* by the end of the first act.

senses.gloss: To crowd close together, usually because of cold or fear.
senses.ru: жаться друг к другу, сбиваться в кучу; прижаться
examples: We *huddled* around the fire until the rain stopped.
Penguins *huddle* to stay warm.
Passengers were *huddling* under the shelter waiting for the bus.

senses.gloss: To stay very close to the edge or surface of something.
examples: The road *hugs* the coastline for twenty miles.
The little car *hugged* the curves all the way down.
Fog was *hugging* the ground when we set out.

senses.gloss: To be full of busy activity.
examples: The kitchen *hums* on Saturday nights.
The office *hummed* with rumors all week.
By noon the market was *humming* with shoppers.

senses.gloss: To search hard for something you need or have lost.
senses.ru: искать, разыскивать; перерыть всё в поисках
examples: I *hunted* everywhere for my keys.
She *hunts* through the closet every single morning.
They are *hunting* for an apartment near the school.

senses.gloss: To make someone move somewhere quickly by pushing or hurrying them.
examples: Two aides *hustled* him through the crowd to the car.
Don't *hustle* me — I'll be ready in a minute.
Security was *hustling* fans toward the exits.

senses.gloss: To work fast and aggressively to make money.
examples: She *hustles* — two jobs and a weekend gig.
He *hustled* for every client on that list.
They have been *hustling* all year to keep the shop open.

senses.gloss: To shut a factory or a workforce down for a period of time.
examples: The strike *idled* four thousand workers.
The plant has been *idled* since June.
A parts shortage is *idling* two assembly lines.

senses.gloss: To make something clear or easy to understand.
examples: A single chart *illuminates* the whole argument.
Her testimony *illuminated* how the money moved.
These letters have *illuminated* a part of his life nobody knew about.

senses.gloss: To think that something is probably true; to suppose.
examples: I *imagine* they'll cancel the flight.
Everyone *imagined* the deal was already done.
I had *imagined* the drive would take about an hour.

senses.gloss: To become completely involved in an activity or a subject.
senses.ru: погружаться, погрузиться (с головой во что-л.); уходить с головой
examples: *Immerse* yourself in the material before the exam.
She *immersed* herself in the language for a year.
He has *immersed* himself in local politics since he retired.

senses.gloss: To give a quality, flavor, or feeling to something.
examples: Oak barrels *impart* a vanilla flavor to the wine.
A pinch of the spice *imparted* a smoky taste.
The low lamps were *imparting* a warm glow to the room.

senses.gloss: To bring a file or data into a program from somewhere else.
examples: You can *import* your contacts from a spreadsheet.
I *imported* the photos into the editor last night.
The app is *importing* your calendar now.

senses.gloss: To make something out of whatever happens to be available.
senses.ru: сооружать на скорую руку, смастерить из подручных средств
examples: Campers learn to *improvise* when they forget something.
They *improvised* a stretcher from two poles and a coat.
She was *improvising* a costume out of an old sheet.

senses.gloss: To have something as one of its parts.
senses.ru: включать в себя, содержать; входить в состав
examples: The price *includes* tax and delivery.
The kit *included* batteries and a charger.
Breakfast is *included* in the room rate.

senses.gloss: To develop quietly inside the body before any symptoms show, said of a disease.
senses.ru: развиваться скрыто, зреть (об инфекции в инкубационный период)
examples: The virus *incubates* for about five days.
Whatever he caught *incubated* for a week and a half.
The infection had been *incubating* long before he felt sick.

senses.gloss: To tie a payment or a rate to the level of prices or to another measure.
examples: The contract *indexes* wages to the consumer price index.
Congress *indexed* the credit to the cost of living.
Benefits are *indexed* to inflation every January.

senses.gloss: To say something briefly or indirectly rather than stating it outright.
senses.ru: давать понять, дать понять; сообщать, заявлять
examples: Sources *indicate* that the deal is close.
The mayor *indicated* she would run again.
Officials have *indicated* that no decision has been made.

senses.gloss: To spread a feeling or a mood to other people.
examples: His enthusiasm *infected* the whole team.
Panic *infects* a trading floor in minutes.
The bad mood was *infecting* everyone in the room.

senses.gloss: To make a number, price, or claim bigger than it really is.
examples: He *inflated* his sales numbers to look good.
Hotels *inflate* prices during the festival.
The figures had been *inflated* for years before anyone checked.

senses.gloss: To shape something and give it its character.
examples: Her years as a nurse *inform* everything she writes.
The decision was *informed* by two long studies.
Fresh data is *informing* every choice the team makes.

senses.gloss: To admit someone into a group with a special ceremony.
examples: The club *initiates* new members every fall.
He was *initiated* into the fraternity in October.
They are *initiating* twelve students tonight.

senses.gloss: To add a new quality or element to something.
examples: She *injected* some humor into a very dull meeting.
The loan *injected* cash into the business at the right moment.
The new coach is *injecting* energy into the team.
